analysis: Both units are base-side excerpts (lines 5075-6861) of fixtures/prompt-contract/v1/production_vectors.json. They contain synthetic, public-text golden vectors (multi_system, nulls, reasoning_effort, response_text): request/provider/template inputs, cache block-boundary chain hashes, and token IDs. All prompt content is explicitly public placeholder text; no secrets, keys, tokens or real consumer data are present. The patch excerpt visible in file_changes shows head-side changes in earlier regions: additional_context enable_thinking=false added to a template_input, prompt_token_count reduced from 803 to 767, chain hashes recomputed, and token_ids trimmed. These are test-fixture changes with no runtime code, authorization, attestation, encryption or endpoint behavior, so no TB-011/TB-002 control is altered. The fixture is the only visible evidence here. The relevant security-adjacent concern is T-041 (prefix-cache sharing): the fixture-defined block boundaries and chain hashes govern cache-key derivation, so a change in the fixture must match the production implementation in the Swift provider and the coordinator or cache keys diverge. The consuming implementation of the prompt-contract/cache planner, and the changed enable_thinking template behavior, were not supplied. I could not verify that cross-tenant cache isolation (scope_id) is unchanged; the visible vectors still use a fixed scope_id of fixture-scope. The head-side hunks past the first patch excerpt, which are truncated, were not examined. No concrete regression is identified from the supplied evidence.
